_comment: Games known to block or punish third-party overlays / code drawn into the game (QA.56). Curated by hand and updated with releases. A listed game keeps the in-game overlay off by default even when it is globally on; turning it on needs an explicit, confirmed override. 'reason' is shown to the user (English, plain text). 'source' must point to the publisher's or anti-cheat vendor's statement, or to the best public report available.

games.name: VALORANT
games.reason: Riot Vanguard is a kernel-level anti-cheat that blocks software it considers unsafe from loading into the game and reports it.

games.name: League of Legends
games.reason: Since 2024 League of Legends uses Riot Vanguard, which blocks software it considers unsafe from loading into the game.

games.name: Call of Duty (Modern Warfare II/III, Warzone, Black Ops 6)
games.reason: Ricochet's kernel-level driver monitors software that interacts with Call of Duty while the game runs; unknown programs drawing into the game risk being flagged.

games.name: Counter-Strike 2 (FACEIT matches)
games.reason: Matches on FACEIT run under FACEIT's kernel-level anti-cheat, which detects overlays and only allows a few known ones (Steam, NVIDIA). Valve's own matchmaking (VAC) does not forbid overlays.

games.name: PUBG: BATTLEGROUNDS
games.reason: PUBG blocks third-party programs that hook into the game or change its visuals (for example ReShade) through BattlEye.

games.name: Apex Legends
games.reason: Easy Anti-Cheat closes Apex Legends when it finds files or programs it cannot verify; EA support advises closing overlays when that happens.
